tables.name: district_indicators
tables.description: Every district-level indicator in Data Darbar, one row per district × indicator × year.
tables.notes: Long format so heterogeneous sources share one table. Filter `kind = 'indicator'` for the measures themselves; kind='quality' rows carry the sample size and small-n flag for the same prefix, and kind='provenance' rows record borrowed estimates. Survey groups suppress cells with n<30 upstream, so an absent row can mean 'suppressed' as well as 'not collected'. DOUBLE-COUNTING TRAP: where a district was split after Census 2017 (see the *_boundary_change provenance rows) both halves carry the SAME 2017 figure for the combined pre-split area, so summing a 2017 count across all districts overstates the total. Filter those rows out, or sum the 2023 year instead.

tables.name: mouza_crosswalk
tables.description: Maps each PBS tehsil to the ADM3 polygon Data Darbar maps it on.
tables.notes: MANY-TO-ONE by design: PBS enumerates 595 tehsils against the boundary file's 553, because it carries sub-tehsils created after the polygons were drawn. Since every Mouza Census figure is a count of mouzas, summing several PBS tehsils into one polygon is the correct operation — group by tehsil_id and sum before taking any share. match records how each row was resolved: exact_name, variant (same place spelled differently), contained, fuzzy, only_tehsil_in_district, parent (a sub-tehsil folded into the unit it was carved from), and approx (no polygon exists for the area, so it was placed in a neighbour — treat those tehsils' placement as a judgement call). All 48,738 mouzas are assigned. The 10 unresolved rows all have zero mouzas.
tables.source: PBS Mouza Census 2020 frame × geoBoundaries PAK ADM3

tables.name: mouza_tehsil
tables.description: Mouza Census 2020 facility counts, one row per PBS tehsil.
tables.notes: Every column is a COUNT OF MOUZAS (revenue villages), never of people or households — a mouza of 12,000 and a mouza of 300 each count once. PBS publishes numerators without a denominator, and its own indicator blocks disagree about how many mouzas answered: only 33 of the 544 enumerated tehsils give a single consistent base, and blocks can differ by up to 181. Take each block's own row sum as its base rather than TotalMauzaCount. Existance/NotExistance pairs are exclusive; drinking water, health facility type, fuel, street surface and media are multiple response, so they can sum past the base. The frame is rural — cities are not revenue villages — but mouzas that urbanise stay in it (4.9% urban, 2.4% partly urban). 51 tehsils return all zeros: AJK and GB were not enumerated, nor were Mand and Tump in Kech or Kallag in Panjgur. Join to the ADM3 geography through mouza_crosswalk. Column names keep PBS's own casing and spelling; DuckDB matches them case-insensitively.
tables.source: PBS Mouza Census 2020 (mc2020.pbos.gov.pk)

tables.description: The macro time-series panel: every observation of every SBP series held here.
tables.notes: One row per series × date. 'U.A.E.' already contains Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Sharjah and 'Other four U.A.E.'s States'; 'Other GCC Countries excluding Saudi Arabia & U.A.E.' already contains Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman and Qatar; 'ten European Countries' already contains Belgium, Denmark, France, Germany, Greece, Ireland, Italy, Netherland, Spain and Sweden — Norway and Switzerland are reported separately. The partition that reconciles exactly to the published total is: Saudi Arabia, U.A.E., U.K., U.S.A., Other GCC, ten European Countries, Norway, Switzerland, Australia, Canada, Japan, Malaysia, South Africa, South Korea, Other Countries. The same shape applies to province-wise banking (TS_GP_BAM_ADVDEP_HY), where 'all Pakistan' is the total of the regional series.

tables.name: school_access_district
tables.description: Distance to the nearest government school by sex, enrolment by sex, and school counts, one row per district (132).
tables.notes: all_km, boys_km, girls_km are POPULATION-WEIGHTED MEDIAN straight-line distances (Lambert conformal conic, km) from every populated 1 km cell to the nearest school of that network; *_min are walking minutes on the Malaria Atlas friction surface. gap_km = girls_km − boys_km (positive = girls further). Networks are by name designation; for Sindh the same medians under the attendance and girls-or-mixed definitions are in girls_km_attend / girls_km_mixed (the designation gap of 0.8 km falls to zero under attendance). tt_caveat flags districts where the friction surface is unreliable (GB) or mountain/desert cells make minutes an upper bound. *_in_school_pct_5_16 are Census 2023 Table 13(b) enrolment rates (enrolled / population aged 5–16) with successor districts summed into parents, so 123 of the 132 rows carry them. living_standards_deprivation_pslm is the (censored) MPI component; material_deprivation_pslm is an uncensored index from PSLM 2019-20 (no toilet, no flush, no piped water, food insecurity). *_n_schools count schools whose POINT falls in the district polygon (the basis of the piece's Figure 1); schools_listed / _with_coords / _in_analysis count rows by the SOURCE's district. The two bases differ where geocoded points cross a boundary. Distances depend on the whole network, not the district's own schools, so a district with few schools can still be close to the next district's.

Sindh networks are by name designation; the designated gap is an upper bound (see school_access_district's mixed and attendance columns). tables.name: school_validation_district
tables.description: External-validity test of the school layer against the Mouza Census 2020, one row per mouza district (147): count floors and village-reported distances.
tables.notes: The Mouza Census asked every rural mouza whether an institution for boys and one for girls exists at each level and, if not, how far the nearest is. tables.name: schools_pk
tables.description: Government schools of Pakistan with positions and provenance, one row per listed school (release 2026-09).
tables.notes: READ coord_method AND coord_precision BEFORE USING lat/lng. Only 82,000 of the 121,000 positioned rows are school-level fixes (GPS at source in Balochistan and KP, RSU pins or positions multilaterated from SELD checker distances in Sindh); 20,000 Punjab, GB and AJK rows sit at the named SETTLEMENT, 8,000 Punjab rows at the MARKAZ (school-cluster) centroid and 9,800 Punjab rows at the TEHSIL centroid — those last two are useless for anything finer than a district. coord_tier is the region's overall grade from the coverage ledger (A to C). in_analysis marks the 118,673 rows that entered Adaad's distance analysis; analysis_note says why the rest did not (no position, closed, sex not stated, not government). gender is the school's name DESIGNATION (GG/GB, Boys/Girls); in Sindh most designated boys' schools are officially Mixed and enrol girls — gender_official carries SEMIS's Boys/Girls/Mixed field and boys_/girls_enrolled the roster's enrolment, so the girls' network can be redefined by attendance. level is the source's own label and level_std collapses it to primary/middle/high; middle_plus and high_plus are the analysis's classes. Coverage: settled KP only (the seven ex-FATA merged districts have no public locations), two of AJK's ten districts, 78 federal schools in Islamabad; see school_layer_coverage. district_key is the source's district mapped to Data Darbar's 147-district frame (successor districts folded into their parent); district_key_boundary is the polygon the point falls in, which is what per-district counts in the piece use — they differ for 3,500 rows. Every position in this table is either published by a provincial education department (Balochistan, KP, and Sindh's pins), solved from distances the Sindh department's own public distance checker returns, or geocoded from a settlement name in a public roster. The table adds nothing a department has not put online: no staff names, no contact details. Released under CC BY 4.0 as a compilation; the underlying records remain the departments'.

examples.title: Ten poorest districts
examples.sql:
SELECT rank, name, prov, mpi, H, A
FROM mpi_districts
WHERE low_n = 0   -- drop districts whose sample is too small to rank
ORDER BY rank LIMIT 10;

examples.title: Female literacy, 2017 vs 2023
examples.sql:
SELECT district, province,
       max(value) FILTER (year = '2017') AS lit_2017,
       max(value) FILTER (year = '2023') AS lit_2023,
       round(max(value) FILTER (year = '2023')
           - max(value) FILTER (year = '2017'), 1) AS change
FROM district_indicators
WHERE indicator = 'literacy_ratio_female'
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY change DESC;

examples.title: Urbanisation vs multidimensional poverty
examples.sql:
SELECT d.district, d.province, d.value AS pct_urban_2023, m.mpi
FROM district_indicators d
JOIN mpi_districts m USING (district_key)
WHERE d.indicator = 'urban_proportion' AND d.year = '2023'
  AND m.low_n = 0
ORDER BY m.mpi DESC;

examples.title: What Pakistan exports most, FY2024-25
examples.sql:
-- country IS NULL rows are the commodity totals; country rows are the
-- partner split of the same money. Never add both.
SELECT hs8, any_value(commodity) AS commodity,
       round(sum(fy_value_kpkr) / 1e6, 1) AS rs_bn
FROM trade_hs8
WHERE direction = 'export' AND fiscal_year = '2024-25'
  AND country IS NULL
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY rs_bn DESC LIMIT 20;

examples.title: Top import partners, FY2024-25 (Rs bn)
examples.sql:
SELECT country, round(sum(fy_value_kpkr) / 1e6, 1) AS rs_bn
FROM trade_hs8
WHERE direction = 'import' AND fiscal_year = '2024-25'
  AND country IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY rs_bn DESC LIMIT 15;

examples.title: Real GDP growth by year
examples.sql:
SELECT year, round(value, 2) AS growth_pct
FROM national_accounts
WHERE table_sheet = 'Table 6' AND item LIKE 'D GDP%'
ORDER BY year;

examples.title: Federal defence budget over time
examples.sql:
-- is_own_year_be keeps the document's own-year budget estimate,
-- the only column that strings into a clean time series.
SELECT doc_fy, item, value_rs_mn
FROM budget_lines
WHERE is_own_year_be AND item ILIKE '%defence%'
ORDER BY doc_fy;

examples.title: Rural electrification, worst tehsils (Mouza Census)
examples.sql:
-- Shares are of MOUZAS, not people. Aggregate to the polygon first:
-- several PBS tehsils can share one boundary.
SELECT x.dd_name AS tehsil, m.province,
       sum(m."ElectrictiyAvailability_NoneMouzas") AS no_electricity,
       sum(m."ElectrictiyAvailability_AllMouzas"
         + m."ElectrictiyAvailability_MostlyMouzas"
         + m."ElectrictiyAvailability_SomeMouzas"
         + m."ElectrictiyAvailability_NoneMouzas") AS base,
       round(100.0 * sum(m."ElectrictiyAvailability_NoneMouzas")
             / nullif(sum(m."ElectrictiyAvailability_AllMouzas"
               + m."ElectrictiyAvailability_MostlyMouzas"
               + m."ElectrictiyAvailability_SomeMouzas"
               + m."ElectrictiyAvailability_NoneMouzas"), 0), 1) AS pct_dark
FROM mouza_tehsil m
JOIN mouza_crosswalk x USING (tehsil_code)
WHERE m.TotalMauzaCount > 0
GROUP BY 1, 2 HAVING base >= 50
ORDER BY pct_dark DESC LIMIT 20;

examples.title: Girls' middle-plus schools by district (Figure 1 of the girls' school piece)
examples.sql:
-- Count by the polygon the point falls in (district_key_boundary), which is
-- how the piece counts; district_key is the register's own district.
SELECT district_key_boundary AS district,
       count(*) FILTER (analysis_sex = 'G') AS girls_schools,
       count(*) FILTER (analysis_sex = 'B') AS boys_schools
FROM schools_pk
WHERE in_analysis AND middle_plus AND district_key_boundary IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY girls_schools DESC;

examples.title: How precise are the positions, by province?
examples.sql:
-- Never map Punjab's tehsil-centroid rows as if they were GPS fixes.
SELECT province, coord_precision, count(*) AS schools,
       round(100.0 * count(*) / sum(count(*)) OVER (PARTITION BY province), 1) AS pct
FROM schools_pk
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY province, schools DESC;

examples.title: Sindh: designated boys' schools that enrol girls
examples.sql:
-- In Sindh the name says GB (boys) but SEMIS calls most of them Mixed and the
-- roster shows girls enrolled. This is why the piece reports the Sindh gap
-- under three network definitions.
SELECT district, count(*) AS boys_designated,
       count(*) FILTER (gender_official = 'Mixed') AS officially_mixed,
       count(*) FILTER (girls_enrolled > 0) AS enrolling_girls,
       sum(girls_enrolled) AS girls_in_them
FROM schools_pk
WHERE province = 'Sindh' AND gender = 'Boys' AND functional AND middle_plus
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY girls_in_them DESC;

examples.title: Where girls are furthest from a middle school, and how many are in school
examples.sql:
SELECT district, region, girls_middle_median_km, boys_middle_median_km, gap_km,
       girls_in_school_pct_5_16, boys_in_school_pct_5_16, tt_caveat
FROM school_access_district
ORDER BY girls_middle_median_km DESC LIMIT 20;

examples.title: Does the Mouza Census agree? Districts where the layer fails its floor test
examples.sql:
-- ratio < 1 means fewer schools in the layer than villages reporting one:
-- schools are missing or misclassified. Sindh's girls-v-boys flag fires by
-- construction (see the notes); read the girls' ratio itself.
SELECT region, mouza_district, ratio_midplus_G, ratio_midplus_B, ratio_high_G, flag
FROM school_validation_district
WHERE status = 'matched' AND ratio_midplus_G < 0.9
ORDER BY ratio_midplus_G;

examples.title: Tehsils where girls are furthest from a middle school
examples.sql:
-- Distances depend on the whole region's network, not the tehsil's own
-- schools; Punjab rows are geocoded, so compare them at district scale.
SELECT tehsil, district_key, region, girls_middle_km, boys_middle_km, gap_middle_km,
       girls_middle_schools, girls_middle_over5km_pct
FROM school_access_tehsil
WHERE coord_tier = 'A'   -- GPS-quality positions only
ORDER BY girls_middle_km DESC LIMIT 25;

examples.title: Sindh multilateration: solved positions that disagree with the RSU pin
examples.sql:
-- 24% of RSU pins sit more than 300 m from the position solved from SELD's own
-- distance checker; the table keeps both so the choice can be audited.
SELECT district, name, level, coord_method, coord_resid_m, pin_vs_solved_m, lat, lng
FROM schools_pk
WHERE province = 'Sindh' AND pin_vs_solved_m > 5000
ORDER BY pin_vs_solved_m DESC LIMIT 25;

examples.title: Find a State Bank series by name
examples.sql:
-- sbp_observations is one row per series x date. Start here: find the
-- series, note its unit and frequency, then join on series_key.
SELECT series_key, series_name, unit, frequency, available_since, available_upto
FROM sbp_series_catalog
WHERE series_name ILIKE '%remittance%'
ORDER BY dataset_code, series_key;

examples.title: The rupee against the dollar since 1947
examples.sql:
SELECT o.obs_date, o.value AS pkr_per_usd
FROM sbp_observations o
JOIN sbp_series_catalog c USING (series_key)
WHERE c.dataset_code = 'TS_GP_ER_FAERPKR_M'   -- bank floating average rates, monthly
  AND c.series_name = 'Average Exchange rate of Pak Rupees per U.S. Dollar'
  -- (a sibling series, 'App (+) / Dep (-) ...', holds the monthly % change)
ORDER BY o.obs_date;

examples.title: Where remittances come from, FY2024-25
examples.sql:
-- The country series are hierarchical (U.A.E. contains Dubai/Abu Dhabi/Sharjah,
-- 'Other GCC' contains Bahrain/Kuwait/Oman/Qatar, 'ten European Countries'
-- contains Belgium..Sweden). Summing all of them overstates the total by 42%;
-- these fifteen add up exactly to SBP's published figure.
SELECT replace(c.series_name, 'Workers'' remittances received from ', '') AS source,
       round(sum(o.value)) AS mn_usd
FROM sbp_observations o JOIN sbp_series_catalog c USING (series_key)
WHERE c.dataset_code = 'TS_GP_BOP_WR_M'
  AND o.obs_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-07-01' AND DATE '2025-06-30'
  AND replace(c.series_name, 'Workers'' remittances received from ', '') IN (
    'Saudi Arabia', 'U.A.E.', 'U.K.', 'U.S.A.',
    'Other GCC Countries excluding Saudi Arabia & U.A.E.', 'ten European Countries',
    'Norway', 'Switzerland', 'Australia', 'Canada', 'Japan', 'Malaysia',
    'South Africa', 'South Korea', 'Other Countries')
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY mn_usd DESC;
